items.title: (a) String Plucked at its Middle Point (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: (a) String Plucked at its Middle Point: a main subheading of 7.5 Stationary waves on a stretched string, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 147-147.

blocks.text: Agar string ko beech (middle point) se chheda jaye to is point se do transverse waves nikalti hain: ek baen sire ki taraf aur doosri daen sire ki taraf jati hai. Jab yeh waves dono clamped (jakre hue) siron tak pohanchti hain to reflect ho kar (palat kar) wapas aati hain aur stationary waves ban jati hain. Dono sire clamped hain, is liye wahan koi motion (harkat) nahi hoti; yani dono siron par nodes bante hain aur beech mein ek antinode, jaisa Fig. 7.7(a) mein hai. Dekhne mein string ek loop mein vibrate karti lagti hai. Do consecutive (saath wale) nodes ka faasla aadhi wavelength hota hai, is liye is mode mein string ki length l yeh hai:

blocks.alt: Do deewaron ke darmiyan jakra length l ka taar ek loop mein jhoolta hai (thos aur dashed curves), Single loop, dono siron par node N aur beech mein antinode A; neeche l = lambda1/2.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.7(a): Vibration ka pehla mode (kitab ki Figure 7.7(a) ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text: Yahan λ₁ is mode mein banne wali waves ki wavelength hai. String mein waves ki speed v string ke tension F aur m (string ka mass per unit length, yaani har metre ka mass) par depend karti hai. String ko kahan se chheda gaya, is se speed par koi farq nahi parta. Speed yeh hai:

Yani vibration ke pehle mode (Fig. 7.7 a) mein is string par sirf frequency f₁ ki waves banti hain.
